spans.s:
तप् 1. तप् [cf. 2. पत्], cl. 4. A. तप्यते,
&c., to rule, govern.

तप् 2. तप्, cl. 1. P. (rarely A.) तपति,
-ते, तताप, तप्स्यति (ep. also तपिष्यति),
अताप्सीत्, तप्तुम्, to give out heat, be hot; to
shine; to heat, make hot or warm; to shine upon;
to be burnt; to burn, to consume or destroy by
heat; to suffer pain; to cause pain or distress; to
injure, hurt, damage, spoil; to torment one's self,
mortify the body, undergo penance, (often with
तपस्, e. g. तपस् तताप, he performed penance);
cl. 4. P. तप्यति (rarely used), to warm one's self,
become hot: Pass. तप्यते, to be heated, to suffer
or feel pain; to be injured or hurt; to suffer pain
voluntarily, undergo severe penances, (often with
तपस्, e. g. तपस् तप्यामहे, we undergo penance);
Caus. P. A. तापयति, -ते, -यितुम्, to make warm
or hot; to burn, consume by heat, cause pain,
trouble, distress; to torment one's self, undergo
penance: Desid. तितप्सति, -ते: Intens. तातप्यते,
तातप्ति, to feel violent pain, suffer torment, be in
great anxiety or distress; [cf. Lat. tepeo: Gr. τέφρα,
rt. ταφ, θάπτω: Russ. tepl, ‘warm;’ teplota,
‘warmth:’ Hib. tebhot, ‘intense heat:’ Old Germ.
damf: Lat. tempus ?].
3. तप्, प्, प्, प्, warming one's self; [cf. अग्नि-तप्.]

तप, अस्, आ, अम्, warming; burning, consuming
by heat [cf. ललाटन्-तप]; causing pain or trouble,
distressing [cf. जनन्-तप and परन्-तप]; (अस्),
m. heat, warmth, fire [cf. आ-तप]; the sun; the
hot season; religious austerity, penance, mortifica-
tion (= तपस्); a peculiar form of fire which
generated the seven mothers of Skanda; N. of one
of the attendants of Śiva; (आ), f., N. of one of the
eight deities of the Bodhi-druma; [cf. अ-तप and
ताप.]
—तप-रुज्, क्, f. the pain of penance.
—त-
पात्मक (˚प-आत्˚), अस्, इका, अम्, practising austeri-
ties.
—तपात्यय (˚प-अत्˚), अस्, m. the end of the
heat, the beginning of the rainy season.
—तपान्त
(˚प-अन्˚), अस्, m. the end of the heat, the beginning
of the rainy season.

ताप ताप, अस्, m. (fr. rt. 2. तप्), heat,
glow, burning, torment, pain (mental or physical);
fever; sorrow, affliction, distress; (ई), f., N. of the
Taptī or Surat river; N. of the Yamunā or Jumnā
river; [cf. पश्चात्-ताप.]
—ताप-हर, अस्, ई, अम्,
removing heat; cooling; consoling, alleviating distress;
(ई), f. a dish, a sort of soup of pulse and grain, first
fried with ghee and turmeric and afterwards boiled
with salt and sugar.
—तापी-ज or तापी-समुद्भव,
अस्, आ, अम्, produced near or occurring near the
river Taptī; pyrites or another kind of mineral
substance; a kind of gem.
—तापेश्वर-तीर्थ
(˚प-ईश्˚), अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha.
—ताप्य्-उत्थ-
सञ्ज्ञक, अम्, n. = ताप्य below.

तपत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, heating or warming; per-
forming penance &c.
—तपताम्-पति, इस्, m. ‘the
chief of burners,’ the sun.

तपती, f. ‘the warming one,’ N. of a daughter
of the Sun and of his wife Chāyā, married to Saṃ-
varaṇa and mother of Kuru; N. of a river, commonly
called Taptī; [cf. तापत्य.]

तपन, अस्, आ, अम्, warming, burning, shining,
an epithet of the sun; causing pain or distress; (अस्),
m. the sun; N. of a divine being (perhaps the sun)
who fights with Garuḍa; N. of one of the five fires in
the Svāhā-kāra; N. of a Rakṣas; a N. of Agastya;
heat, burning, the hot season; N. of a burning hell;
N. of several plants, viz. Semecarpus Anacardium
[cf. अरुष्-कर]; Calotropis Gigantea (अर्क), the
white variety of it; Premna Spinosa (क्षु-
द्राग्नि-मन्थ); Cassia Senna; the sun-stone [cf.
सूर्य-कान्त, तपन-मणि, तपनोपल]; (ई), f.
heat; the root of Bignonia Suaveolens; N. of a
river, = तापी and तपनात्मजा, according to some
authorities = गोदावरी; (अम्), n. the being hot,
burning; pining, grieving, mental distress; [cf. राम-
तपन, ‘the distress of Rāma,’ N. of an Upaniṣad;
त्रिपुरा-त्˚, गोपाल-त्˚; cf. also तापन.]
—तपन-
कर, अस्, m. a ray, a sunbeam.
—तपन-च्छद,
अस्, m. the sunflower, = आदित्य-पत्त्र.
—तपन-
तनय, अस्, m. ‘the son of the Sun,’ a N. of Karṇa;
(आ), f. ‘the daughter of the Sun,’ the Yamunā river;
the Taptī river [cf. तपनात्मजा]; N. of a tree;
[cf. शमी.]
—तपन-मणि, इस्, m. the sun-stone;
[cf. सूर्य-कान्त.]
—तपनांशु (˚न-अं˚), उस्,
m. a ray of the sun, a sunbeam.
—तपनात्मजा
(˚न-आत्म-जा), f. ‘the daughter of the Sun,’ N. of a
river, = तपनी and तापी, according to some authori-
ties = गोदावरी [cf. तपनी and तपन], and
यमुना.
—तपनेष्ट (˚न-इष्˚), अम्, n. copper
(‘loved by the rays of the sun,’ i. e. easily heated or
coloured by them).
—तपनोपल (˚न-उप्˚), अस्,
m. the sun-stone; [cf. सूर्य-कान्त.]

तापन, अस्, ई, अम्, burning, inflaming, heating,
distressing [cf. इन्द्र-त्˚ and चन्द्र-त्˚]; (अस्), m.
the sun; the hot season; the sun-stone [cf. सूर्य-
कान्त]; N. of one of the arrows of the god of
love; (अम्), n. burning; distressing, chastising; a
division of hell; gold; [cf. तपन.]

तपनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be heated; to be suffered
or practised as penance; (अम्), n. gold purified with
fire, gold in general; a sort of rice.
—तपनीय-
मय, अस्, ई, अम्, consisting of purified gold, golden.

तापनीय, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. तपनीय), golden,
[]
made of gold; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a school of the
Vājasaneyi-saṃhitā or White Yajur-veda.
—तापनी-
योपनिषद् (˚य-उप्˚), त्, f., N. of an Upaniṣad.
तपनीयक, अम्, n. gold.
तपन्तक, अस्, m., N. of a man.

तपस्, अस्, n. warmth, heat, fire, (पञ्च तपांसि,
the five fires to which an ascetic is exposed in the
hot season, viz. four fires lighted in the several
quarters and the sun burning from above); pain,
suffering; religious austerity, penance, mortification,
the practice of mental or personal self-denial or the
infliction of bodily tortures; the meditation connected
with such a practice; moral virtue, merit; special
observance or duty of any particular caste (e. g. the
Tapas of a Brāhman is sacred learning; of a Kṣa-
triya, the protection of subjects; of a Vaiśya, giving
alms to Brāhmans; of a Śūdra, service; and of a
Ṛṣi or saint, feeding upon herbs and roots); a
particular month of the cold season intervening
between winter and spring (= Māgha or January-
February, the month of religious austerities; cf. त-
पस्य); one of the seven worlds, the region above
the Jana-loka, inhabited by saints or devotees after
death [cf. तपो-लोक]; (in astrology) the ninth lunar
mansion, = धर्म; N. of a long period of time, a
Kalpa; (आस्, अस्), m. n. the cold or dewy season (=
शिशिर); the winter (= हिमर्तु); the hot season.
—तपः-कर, अस्, आ, अम्, undergoing religious
austerities or penance &c.; (अस्), m. a kind of fish,
Polynemus Risua or Paradiseus, (this fish is also
called Tapasyā-matsya); [cf. तपस्-विन्.]
—तपः-
कृश, अस्, आ, अम् emaciated by austerities.
—तपः-
क्लेश-सह, अस्, आ, अम्, patient of austerities, enduring
the pain of penance.
—तपः-प्रभाव, अस्, m. the
efficacy of devotion.
—तपः-शील, अस्, आ, अम्, in-
clined to religious austerities.
—तपः-समाधि, इस्,
m. the practice of penance.
—तपः-साध्य, अस्, आ,
अम्, to be accomplished by penance.
—तपः-सिद्ध,
अस्, आ, अम्, accomplished by penance.
—तपः-स्थली,
f. ‘the seat of religious austerity or piety,’ a N. of
Benares.
—तपश्-चरण, अम्, n. or तपश्-चर्या,
f. the practice of penance.
—तपश्-चित्, त्, त्, त्, accu-
mulating religious merit by austerities; (तस्), m. pl.,
N. of a class of deities; तपश्चिताम् अयनम्, N.
of a religious ceremony which lasts several days.
—तपसो-मूर्ति, इस्, m., N. of one of the seven
sages in the twelfth Manv-antara; [cf. तपो-मूर्ति.]
—तपस्-तक्ष, अस्, m. ‘destroying religious
penance,’ an epithet of Indra as disturbing the
austerities of ascetics lest they should acquire too
great power; (other authorities explain the word
‘emaciating himself by his devotions;’ and others
read तपस्-तङ्क, ‘afraid of austerities’ or ‘the axe
of austerities.’)
—तपस्-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a
place of pilgrimage.
—तपस्-पति, इस्, m. the lord
of penance.
—तपस्-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. burning,
hot; ascetic, devout; [cf. तपो-वत्.]
—तपस्वि-ता,
f. devout austerity, religious penance, bodily morifica-
tion.
—तपस्-विन्, ई, इनी, इ, distressed, wretched,
poor, miserable, pitiable; practising austerities, de-
vout; a mendicant, a pauper; an ascetic, a religious
man engaged in the practice of rigorous and devout
penance; (ई), m., N. of a son of Manu Cākṣuṣa
and Naḍvalā; N. of one of the seven sages of the
twelfth Manv-antara; an epithet of Nārada; the
mango fish, Polynemus Risua [cf. तपः-कर]; N.
of a tree, a kind of Karañja (घृत-करञ्ज);
(इनी), f. a female devotee, a woman leading a re-
ligious life; a poor wretched woman; spikenard,
Valeriana Jaṭāmānsi; another plant, Helleborus Niger,
= कटु-रोहिणी; also = महा-श्रावणिका.
—तप-
स्वि-पत्त्र, अस्, m., N. of a plant, = दमनक; [cf.
तपो-धन.]
—तपो-जा, आस्, आस्, अम्, Ved. born from
heat; one who practises religious austerities.
—तपो-
द, अस्, आ, अम्, granting piety; (अम्), n., N. of a
Tīrtha in Magadha.
—तपो-दान, अम्, n., N. of a
Tīrtha.
—तपो-धन, अस्, आ, अम्, rich in religious
penance; ascetic, pious; a very treasure of mortifica-
tions and austerities, a devotee, an ascetic, performing
religious penance; consisting in religious penance;
[]
granting religious merit or piety; (अस्), m., N. of a
son of Manu Tāmasa; N. of a plant, = दमनक,
commonly दवणा, Artemisia [cf. तपस्वि-पत्त्र];
(आ), f. the plant Sphæranthus Mollis, = मुण्डीरी,
commonly मुण्डी.
—तपो-धर्म, अस्, m., N. of
a son of the thirteenth Manu.
—तपो-धामन्, अ,
n. ‘the abode of penance,’ N. of a place of pilgrimage.
—तपो-धृति, इस्, m., N. of one of the seven sages
of the twelfth Manv-antara.
—तपो-नित्य, अस्, आ, अम्,
devoting one's self uninterruptedly to religious auste-
rities or penance; (अस्), m., N. of a man with the
patronymic Pauruśiṣṭi.
—तपो-निधि, इस्, m. a
treasury of religious austerities and penance, a very
treasure of merit derived from self-mortification, an
eminently pious man.
—तपो-निष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम्,
performing penance, practising austerities.
—तपो-
ऽनुभाव (˚पस्-अन्˚), अस्, m. the influence of re-
ligious penance.
—तपो-बल, अम्, n. the power
acquired by religious austerities.
—तपो-भङ्ग,
अस्, m. interruption of religious penance.
—तपो-
भृत्, त्, त्, त्, undergoing penance, ascetic, pious; an
ascetic, a pious man.
—तपो-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, con-
sisting in religious penance, containing it; practising
austerities, devout.
—तपो-मूर्ति, इस्, f. an incarna-
tion of religious austerity or penance; an ascetic;
(इस्), m., N. of one of the seven sages of the twelfth
Manv-antara; [cf. तपसो-मूर्ति.]
—तपो-मूल,
अस्, आ, अम्, founded on religious austerity or penance;
(अस्), m., N. of a son of Manu Tāmasa.
—तपो-
युक्त, अस्, आ, अम्, employed in penitential exercises,
ascetic, pious.
—तपो-रति, इस्, इस्, इ, rejoicing in re-
ligious austerity; (इस्), m., N. of a son of Manu
Tāmasa.
—तपो-रवि, इस्, m. ‘the sun of the ascetics,’
N. of one of the seven sages in the twelfth Manv-
antara.
—तपो-राज, अस्, m. ‘king of penance,’ the
moon.
—तपो-राशि, इस्, m. ‘a heap of religious
austerities;’ an ascetic.
—तपो-लोक, अस्, m. one of
the seven worlds, that which is situated above the
Jana-loka; [cf. तपस्.]
—तपो-वट, अस्, m. ‘en-
closure or district of religious penance,’ a N. applied
to Brahmāvarta, i. e. the holy land situated in central
India.
—तपो-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, ascetic, pious; [cf.
तपस्-वत्.]
—तपो-वन, अस्, m. ‘penance-grove,’
a sacred grove in which ascetics perform their re-
ligious austerities.
—तपो-वास, अस्, m. a place of
religious austerity.
—तपो-विशेष, अस्, m. excellence
of devotion.
—तपो-वृद्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, rich in
religious austerity or penance, very ascetic or pious.
—तपो-व्रात, अस्, m. a multitude of penances.
—तपो-ऽशन (˚पस्-अश्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, one whose
food is religious austerity; (अस्), m., N. of one of
the seven sages of the twelfth Manv-antara; also of
a son of Manu Tāmasa.
तपसीवन्, आ, अरी, अ, causing pain (?).

1. तपस्य, nom. P. तपस्यति, to undergo reli-
gious austerities, do penance.

2. तपस्य, अस्, आ, अम्, produced by heat; (अस्),
m. the month Phālguna (February-March), the
second month of the season intervening between
winter and spring; a N. of Arjuna; N. of a son of
Manu Tāmasa; (आ), f. devout austerity, religious
penance; (अम्), n. devout austerity, mortification,
religious penance; the flower of Jasminum Multi-
florum or Pubescens (कुन्द-पुष्प).
—तपस्या-
मत्स्य, the mango fish; [cf. under तपः-कर.]

तापस्य, अम्, n. asceticism, the condition of a
devotee, penance.
तपित, अस्, आ, अम्, heated, burnt, refined.

तापित, अस्, आ, अम्, heated, inflamed, distressed,
pained.

तपिष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. 2. तप् with the superl.
affix), Ved. extremely hot, burning; [cf. तपीयस्.]
तपिष्णु, उस्, उस्, उ, warming, heating, burning.

तपीयस्, आन्, असी, अस् (fr. 2. तप् with the compar.
affix), extremely ascetic, most devoted to religious
austerities.
तपु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. burning hot.
तपुषि, इस्, इस्, इ, Ved. burning.
तपुषी, f. the heat of anger or wrath.

तपुस्, उस्, उस्, उस्, Ved. burning hot; (उस्), m.
fire; the sun; an enemy (who causes pain); (उस्),
n. heat, pain.
—तपुर्-अग्र, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. having
a burning point or extremity (as a spear).
—तपुर्-
जम्भ, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. having burning jaws, an
epithet of Agni.
—तपुर्-मूर्धन्, आ, आ, अ, Ved.
[]
having a burning head, an epithet of Agni; (आ), m.,
N. of an author of a hymn of the Ṛg-veda who was
a son of Bṛhaspati.
—तपुर्-वध, अस्, आ, अम्,
Ved. having burning weapons.
—तपुष्-पा, आस्, आस्,
अम्, Ved. (Sāy.) protecting from pain; (perhaps
rather) drinking warm (beverages).

तप्त, अस्, आ, अम्, heated, inflamed, burnt; hot;
red-hot; fused, melted, molten; burnished; scorched
by pain or sorrow, distressed, afflicted; inflamed with
anger, incensed; undergone or performed (as penance).
—तप्त-कुम्भ, अस्, m. a heated or red-hot jar;
N. of a particular hell; (अस्, आ, अम्), having hot jars.
—तप्त-कूप, ‘hot-well,’ N. of a hell; (perhaps a
wrong reading for the preceding.)
—तप्त-कृच्छ्र,
अस्, अम्, m. n. a sort of penance which consists in
drinking hot water, milk, and ghee for three days
each, and inhaling hot air for three days.
—तप्त-
तपस्, आस्, m. one who has performed penance, an
ascetic.
—तप्त-पाषाण-कुण्ड, अम्, n. ‘a pit
filled with burning stones,’ N. of a hell.
—तप्त-
बालुक, अस्, आ, अम्, having hot or burning gravel;
(अस्), m., N. of a hell.
—तप्त-रूप or तप्त-
रूपक, अम्, n. silver.
—तप्त-लोमश, green
vitriol.
—तप्त-लोह, अम्, n. ‘glowing iron,’ N. of
a hell.
—तप्त-शूर्मि or तप्त-सूर्मि, इस्, f. ‘a red-
hot iron statue,’ N. of a hell in which the wicked are
made to embrace red-hot images.
—तप्तशूर्मि-
कुण्ड, अम्, n., N. of a hell.
—तप्त-सुरा-कुण्ड,
अस्, m. ‘a jar or hole filled with burning spirituous
liquor,’ N. of a hell.
—तप्त-हेम-मय, अस्, ई, अम्,
like or consisting of melted gold.
—तप्तान्न (˚त-
अन्˚), अम्, n. hot food, hot rice.
—तप्तायन (˚त-
अय्˚), अस्, ई, अम्, Ved. serving as a dwelling-place for
the distressed (as the earth).

तप्तव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be performed as a reli-
gious penance.

तप्तृ, ता, त्री, तृ, making warm or hot, heating,
a heater.

तप्त्वा, ind. having heated, having performed
penance.

तप्य, अस्, आ, अम्, performing religious austerity,
doing penance.

ताप्य, अस्, अम्, m. n. or ताप्यक, अम्, n. a
mineral substance, sulphuret of iron.
तप्यति, इस्, f., Ved. heat.
तप्यतु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. hot, glowing.

तप्स्यत्, अन्, अती or अन्ती, अत्, practising or intend-
ing to practise austerities.

तपश तपश, अस्, m. the moon; [cf. the
following.]

तपस तपस, अस्, m. (said to be fr. 2. तप्),
the moon; a bird; [cf. the preceding.]

तापस, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. तपस्), performing pe-
nance, a practiser of austerities; devout; a hermit;
a devotee, an ascetic; relating to religious penance
or to an ascetic; (अस्), m., N. or epithet of a Hotṛ;
a kind of crane, Ardea Nivea, = वक; a kind of
sugar-cane; a kind of plant, = दमनक; (ई), f., N.
of two plants, viz. Curcuma Zedoaria and Jaṭāmāṃsī;
(अम्), n. the leaf of the Laurus Cassia, = तमाल-
पत्त्र; [cf. तापस-ज.]
—तापस-ज, अम्, n. the
leaf of the Laurus Cassia.
—तापस-तरु, उस्, m. or
तापस-द्रुम, अस्, m. the tree of the ascetics,
Terminalia Catappa [cf. इङ्गुद] or Putranjiva
Roxburghii.
—तापसद्रुम-सन्निभा, f. a kind
of plant, = गर्भ-दात्री.
—तापस-पत्त्री, f. the
plant Artemisia Indica.
—तापस-प्रिय, अस्, आ, अम्,
dear to ascetics; (अस्), m. the tree Buchanania Lati-
folia, = प्रियाल; (आ), f. a kind of sugar-cane; a
grape; Ganitrus Sphærica; Chironia Sapida, = रुद्रा-
क्ष.
—तापस-वृक्ष, अस्, m. = तापस-तरु.
—तापसाध्युषित (˚स-अध्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, in-
habited by hermits.
—तापसारण्य (˚स-अर्˚), अम्,
n. a wood of hermits.
—तापसेष्ट (˚स-इष्˚), अस्,
m. the tree Buchanania Latifolia.

तापक, अस्, आ, अम्, heating, burning, inflaming;
(अस्), m. fever, morbid heat.

तापत्य, अस्, आ, अम्, relating to Tapatī (q. v.),
treating of her; a metronymic from Tapatī, epithet
of Kuru, also of Arjuna.

तापयान, अस्, आ, अम्, warming, burning, illu-
minating.

तापायन, आस्, m. pl., N. of a school of the
Vājasaneyi-saṃhitā or White Yajur-veda.

तापयिष्णु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. heating, burning,
causing pain.

तापश्चित, अम्, n. (fr. तपश्-चित्), N. of a sacri-
ficial ceremony of long continuance; (अस्, ई, अम्), an
epithet of the sacrificial fire used at this ceremony.
तापिक in जल-तापिक, q. v.

तापिन्, ई, इनी, इ, oppressed by heat, morbid, suf-
fering from disease (moral or physical); anything
heated or glowing; (ई), m. one of the deified saints
of the Buddhists; (इनी), f. a N. of the letter व्;
[cf. जल-तापिक.]

तापिच्छ तापिच्छ or तापिञ्छ, अस्, m. the
plant Xanthochymus Pictorius; [cf. तमाल.]

तापिञ्ज, अस्, m. the plant Xanthochymus Pictorius;
(अम्), n. = तापीज, ताप्य, sulphuret of iron.

तापितट तापितट or तीपीतट or तापीतट-
देश, अस्, m., N. of a country.

तापीमाहात्म्य तापी-माहात्म्य, अम्, n., N. of
a part of the Skanda-Purāṇa.
तपर्-लोक = तपो-लोक.
